<p style="font-size:16px;">We all use the general libraries for data analysis and model fitting, but a nice thing with R is that you can interface any function with others. And a bunch of packages have been developed with ecological research in mind. Recently, <a href="http://schamberlain.github.com/2012/06/recent-r-eeb-packages/">Scott Chamberlain</a> posted a good  summary of new R libraries specifically useful for ecologists.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://www.zoology.ubc.ca/~schluter/bio548/rtips.html">Dolph Schluter</a>‘s page and <a href="http://dyerlab.bio.vcu.edu/downloads/Dyer_Data_Analysis_Using_R.pdf">Rodney Dyer</a>‘s page have interesting tips for using R in evolutionary ecology and population genetics, respectively. An additional R resource for ecologists is the <a href="http://www.nceas.ucsb.edu/scicomp/software/r">R programming resource center at NCEAS</a> and the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Environmetrics.html">CRAN Task View for Analysis of Ecological and Environmental Data</a>. Finally, ecological analysis with R was the core subject of a special issue of the <a href="http://www.jstatsoft.org/v22/">Journal of Statistical Software</a> in 2007.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;">Here is my summary of useful R packages for ecologists. I’m including here those packages that I consider more directly related to ecology and that I’ve used most. Obviously we all use many R packages for ecological research, but the idea here is to summarize those that specifically address ecological research. Some of those libraries might remain “hidden” amidst the zillions of libraries available in R. useRs interested in ecological research should consult additional <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/">R Task Views</a>, such as the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Spatial.html">Spatial</a> view. Additional interesting stuff for ecologists is also available in the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Genetics.html">Genetics</a>, <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Multivariate.html">Multivariate</a>, <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Phylogenetics.html">Phylogenetics</a> and <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Cluster.html">Cluster</a> task views, among others.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><strong>General libraries for ecological research, with multiple functions</strong></span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ade4/index.html"><tt>ade4</tt></a>. Analysis of ecological data with exploratory and euclidean methods in environmental sciences. Basically a series of functions for multivariate data analysis and graphics. true web page is <a href="http://pbil.univ-lyon1.fr/ade4/home.php?lang=eng">here</a>. It also has a GUI (graphic user interface), <a href="http://pbil.univ-lyon1.fr/ade4TkGUI/">ade4TkGUI</a>.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adehabitatHR/index.html"><tt>adehabitatHR</tt></a>. A collection of tools for the estimation of home range in animals.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adehabitatHS/index.html"><tt>adehabitatHS</tt></a>. A collection of tools for the analysis of habitat selection by animals.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adehabitatLT/index.html"><tt>adehabitatLT</tt></a>. A collection of tools for the analysis of animal movement patterns.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/BiodiversityR/index.html"><tt>BiodiversityR</tt></a>. Statistical analysis of biodiversity patterns. This is a GUI (Graphical User Interface, via the <a href="http://www.rcommander.com/">R-Commander</a>) and some utility functions (often based on the vegan package) for statistical analysis of biodiversity and ecological communities, including species accumulation curves, diversity indices, Renyi profiles, GLMs for analysis of species abundance and presence-absence, distance matrices, Mantel tests, and cluster, constrained and unconstrained ordination analysis. A book on biodiversity and community ecology analysis is available for free download from the website.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vegan/index.html"><tt>vegan</tt></a>.</span> Ordination methods, diversity analysis and other functions for community and vegetation ecologists.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ecodist/index.html"><tt>ecodist</tt></a>.</span> Dissimilarity-based analysis functions including ordination and Mantel test functions, intended for use with spatial and community data.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bio.infer/index.html"><tt>bio.infer</tt></a>.</span> Predict environmental conditions from biological observations.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/meta/index.html"><tt>meta</tt></a>. Functions for meta.analysis. Fixed and random effects meta-analysis. Functions for tests of bias, forest and funnel plot.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mra/index.html"><tt>mra</tt></a>. Analysis of mark-recapture data using covariates. Models: CJS open population; Huggin’s closed population. Link functions: logit, sine, hazard. Model selection and model averaging routines. Plot methods. Simulation routine. CJS methods produce estimates of population size using the Horvitz-Thompson estimator.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/popbio/index.html"><tt>popbio</tt></a>. Analysis of matrix population models. Construct and analyze projection matrix models from a demography study of marked individuals classified by age or stage. The package covers methods described in Matrix Population Models by Caswell (2001) and Quantitative Conservation Biology by Morris and Doak (2002).</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://lib.stat.cmu.edu/S/Harrell/help/Hmisc/html/Overview.html"><tt>Hmisc</tt></a>. Functions useful for ecological data analysis, high-level graphics, utility operations, computing sample size and power, imputing missing values, advanced table making, etc.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vegclust/index.html"><tt>vegclust</tt></a>. Fuzzy clustering of vegetation data. This package contains functions used to perform fuzzy clustering of vegetation data under different models.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://goo.gl/em18O" target="_blank" title="demoniche"><tt>demoniche</tt></a>. An R-package for simulating spatially-explicit population dynamics. Nenzén et al. 2012. Ecography, 35: 577–580. doi: 10.1111/j.1600-0587.2012.07378.x.</p>
<p><a href="http://r-forge.r-project.org/R/?group_id=302" target="_blank" title="BioMod"><tt>BioMod</tt></a>. Functions for ensemble forecasting of species distributions, enabling the treatment of a range of methodological uncertainties in models and the examination of species-environment relationships. Thuillier et al. 2009. Ecography 32, 369–373. doi: 10.1111/j.1600-0587.2008.05742.x.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/simecol/index.html"><tt>simecol</tt></a>. Simulation of ecological (and other) dynamic systems. Object oriented framework to simulate ecological (and other) dynamic systems. It can be used for differential equations, individual-based (or agent-based) and other models as well. The package helps to organize scenarios (avoids copy and paste) and improves readability and usability of code.</p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/fossil/index.html"><tt>fossil</tt></a>. Palaeoecological and palaeogeographical analysis tools. A set of analytical tools useful in analysing ecological and geographical data sets, both ancient and modern. The package includes functions for estimating species richness (Chao 1 and 2, ACE, ICE, Jacknife), shared species/beta diversity, species area curves and geographic distances and areas.</p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><strong>Spatial ecology.</strong> Also see the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Spatial.html">Spatial R Task View</a>.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spatstat/index.html"><span style="font-family:Courier;"><tt>spatstat</tt></span></a>.</span> A package for analysing spatial data, mainly Spatial Point Patterns, including multitype/marked points and spatial covariates, in any two-dimensional spatial region. Also supports three-dimensional point patterns, and space-time point patterns in any number of dimensions.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spdep/index.html"><tt>spdep</tt></a>. Spatial dependence: weighting schemes, statistics and models. A collection of functions to create spatial weights matrix objects from polygon contiguities, from point patterns by distance and tesselations, for summarising these objects, and for permitting their use in spatial data analysis, including regional aggregation by minimum spanning tree; a collection of tests for spatial autocorrelation, including global Moran’s I, APLE, Geary’s C, Hubert/Mantel general cross product statistic, etc.</p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ecespa/index.html"><tt>ecespa</tt></a>. Functions for spatial point pattern analysis. Some wrappers, functions and data sets for for spatial point pattern analysis (mainly based on spatstat), used in the book “Introducción al Análisis Espacial de Datos en Ecología y Ciencias Ambientales: Métodos y Aplicaciones”, by Marcelino de la Cruz.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spatial/index.html"><tt>spatial</tt></a>. Functions for kriging and point pattern analysis.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/SpatialEpi/index.html"><tt>SpatialEpi</tt></a>. Various spatial epidemiological analyses. Cluster detection, disease mapping.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/geoR/index.html"><tt>geoR</tt></a>. Analysis of geostatistical data. Geostatistical analysis including traditional, likelihood-based and Bayesian methods.</span></p>
<p><strong>Molecular ecology</strong><span style="font-size:16px;">. Also see the </span><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Genetics.html" style="font-size:16px;">Genetics R Task View</a><span style="font-size:16px;">. useRs interested in ecological genomics should have a look to </span><a href="http://www.bioconductor.org/" style="font-size:16px;">Bioconductor</a><span style="font-size:16px;"> and the </span><a href="http://rgenetics.org/" style="font-size:16px;">RGenetics Project</a><span style="font-size:16px;">.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/Geneland/index.html"><tt>Geneland</tt></a>. Functions for detecting spatial structures from genetic data within a Bayesian framework via MCMC estimation.</span></p>
<p style="font-size:16px;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adegenet/index.html"><tt>adegenet</tt></a>. Implements a number of different methods for analysing population structure using multivariate statistics, graphics and spatial statistics.</span></p>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/genetics/index.html"><tt>genetics</tt></a>. Implements classes and methods for representing genotype and haplotype data, and has several functions for population genetic analysis (e.g. functions for estimation and testing of Hardy-Weinberg and linkage disequilibria, etc.).</span></div>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><br/>
</span></div>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><tt><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/HardyWeinberg/index.html">HardyWeinberg</a></tt>. Graphical representation of HW disequilibria via ternary plots.</span></div>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><br/>
</span></div>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/qtl/index.html"><tt>qtl</tt></a>. QTL analysis and genome-wide scans.</span></div>
<div><span style="font-size:16px;"><br/>
</span></div>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><strong>Network ecology</strong> </span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;">I don’t like the name ‘network ecology’, but you probably know what I mean. R libraries developed by social scientists (e.g., sna) provide many useful functions for ecological research.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bipartite/index.html"><tt>bipartite</tt></a>. Visualising bipartite networks and calculating some (ecological) indices. Bipartite provides functions to visualise webs and calculate a series of indices commonly used to describe pattern in ecological webs. It focusses on webs consisting of only two trophic levels, e.g. pollination webs or predator-prey-webs. Visualisation is important to get an idea of what we are actually looking at, while the indices summarise different aspects of the webs topology.</span></p>
<p><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sna/index.html"><tt>sna</tt></a>. Tools for Social Network Analysis. A range of tools for social network analysis, including node and graph-level indices, structural distance and covariance methods, structural equivalence detection, p* modeling, random graph generation, and 2D/3D network visualization.</p>
<p><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/igraph/index.html"><tt>igraph</tt></a>. Network analysis and visualization. Routines for simple graphs and network analysis. igraph can handle large graphs very well and provides functions for generating random and regular graphs, graph visualization, centrality indices, etc.</p>
<p><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tnet/index.html"><tt>tnet</tt></a>. Analysis of Weighted, Two-mode, and Longitudinal networks.</p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><strong>Evolutionary ecology </strong></span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;">Please see <a href="http://schamberlain.github.com/2012/06/recent-r-eeb-packages/">Scott Chamberlain</a>‘s blog and the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Phylogenetics.html">Phylogenetics</a> view task. A most useful resource is the <a href="http://www.r-phylo.org/wiki/Main_Page">Phylogenetic comparative methods page</a> at <a href="http://www.nescent.org/">NEScent</a>. In addition:</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ape/index.html"><tt>ape</tt></a>. Analyses of phylogenetics and evolution.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/picante/index.html"><tt>picante</tt></a>. Phylocom integration, community analyses, null-models, traits and evolution.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/geiger/index.html"><tt>geiger</tt></a>. Analysis of evolutionary diversification. Running macroevolutionary simulation, and estimating parameters related to diversification from comparative phylogenetic data.</span></p>
<p><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/adephylo/index.html" style="font-size:16px;"><tt>adephylo</tt></a><span style="font-size:16px;">. Exploratory analyses for the phylogenetic comparative method. </span><span style="font-size:16px;">Multivariate tools to analyze comparative data, i.e. a phylogeny and some traits measured for each taxa., community analyses, null-models, traits and evolution in R.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/spacodiR/index.html"><tt>spacodiR</tt></a>. Spatial and phylogenetic analysis of community diversity. SPACoDi is primarily designed to characterise the structure and phylogenetic diversity of communities using abundance or presence-absence data of species among community plots.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phylobase/index.html"><tt>phylobase</tt></a>. Base package for phylogenetic structures and comparative data.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ouch/index.html"><tt>ouch</tt></a>. Fit and compare Ornstein-Uhlenbeck models for evolution along a phylogenetic tree.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phangorn/index.html"><tt>phangorn</tt></a>. Phylogenetic analysis in R: estimation of phylogenetic trees and networks using maximum likelihood, maximum parsimony, distance methods &amp; Hadamard conjugation.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/paleotree/index.html"><tt>paleotree</tt></a>. Paleontological and phylogenetic analyses of evolution. Analyzes, time-scales and simulates phylogenies of extinct/fossil lineages, along with calculation of diversity curves. Also fits likelihood models to estimate sampling rates from stratigraphic ranges.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phylotools/index.html"><tt>phylotools</tt></a>. Phylogenetic tools for eco-phylogenetics. Building supermatrix for DNA barcodes using different genes, calculating the inequality among lineages and phylogenetic similarity for very large dataset using slicing methods by invoking Phylocom.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><br/>
</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><strong>Note</strong>: To automatically install the <a href="http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/">R Task Views</a> (i.e., groups of packages useful for some specific analysis and pre-bundled in CRAN), the ctv package needs to be installed, e.g.:</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size:16px;"><tt>install.packages("ctv")</tt></span></p>
<p><span style="font-family:monospace;"><span style="font-size:16px;"><tt><tt>library("ctv")</tt></tt></span></span></p>
